No side effects. Called from 0c06d698 together with another env getter (0c067168). The field's meaning is not evidenced in this packet (possibly a connection/link parameter such as an interval or handle).
ble_219_0c066d10.notes: Meaning of the field unknown; name is positional.

ble_219_0c066d20.name: ble_ctrl_env_get_flag_bit6_at_0x18e
ble_219_0c066d20.summary: Return bit 6 of the flag byte at env+0x18E (0 or 1)
ble_219_0c066d20.description: Reads the byte at +0x18e of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0, masks it with 0x7f and shifts right by 6, which yields just bit 6 (0 or 1). Pure getter without side effects. Always called together with ble_ctrl_env_get_u16_at_0x56 (0c066f2c) from 0c06ca3c, 0c06caf4 and 0c06ed64.

ble_219_0c066d34.name: ble_ctrl_env_get_addr_type_and_addr_a
ble_219_0c066d34.summary: Get own address type and 6-byte device address (variant using type flag at env+0x1DC)
ble_219_0c066d34.description: Writes the byte at env+0x1dc to *param_1 (address type: 0 selects the public address). If it is 0 the 6-byte address at env+0x38 (u32 + u16, the public BD_ADDR) is copied to param_2, otherwise the 6-byte address at env+0x1dd..0x1e2 (the alternate/random address) is copied. Used by the caller 0c051eb8, which is an advertising/scan related routine. Env is the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0.

params.name: param_1
params.description: out: address type byte (0 = public, nonzero = random/other)

ble_219_0c066d34.notes: Interpretation as public vs random address type is inferred from the 6-byte layout.

ble_219_0c066d5c.name: ble_ctrl_env_get_addr_type_and_addr_b
ble_219_0c066d5c.summary: Get own address type and 6-byte device address (variant using type flag at env+0x218)
ble_219_0c066d5c.description: Same as ble_ctrl_env_get_addr_type_and_addr_a except that the type byte is read from env+0x218 instead of env+0x1dc: it is stored to *param_1 and, when zero, the public address at env+0x38 (4+2 bytes) is returned in param_2, otherwise the alternate address at env+0x1dd (4+2 bytes). No direct callers (referenced through a function-pointer table). Env is the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0.
ble_219_0c066d5c.notes: Likely the second role/instance counterpart of the 0c066d34 getter.

ble_219_0c066de8.name: ble_ctrl_env_set_iface_and_init

ble_219_0c066de8.description: Stores param_1 into env+0x10 of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0; if non-NULL, treats it as a table of function pointers and calls entry 0 (typically an init/open callback) with no arguments. Called once from the large interface-registration function 0c05b67c.

params.name: param_1

ble_219_0c066ebc.name: ble_ctrl_env_set_callbacks_and_notify

ble_219_0c066ebc.description: Writes param_1 into env+8 of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0. If param_1 is non-NULL and its entry at +4 is non-NULL, that callback is invoked with the value stored at env+4 as the only argument. Called from the registration function 0c05b67c.

params.name: param_1

ble_219_0c066ed4.name: ble_ctrl_env_get_u8_at_0x5a
ble_219_0c066ed4.description: Simple getter returning the byte at +0x5a of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0. Called from 0c06c8f4.

ble_219_0c066efc.name: ble_ctrl_env_set_u8_at_0x59

ble_219_0c066f0c.name: ble_ctrl_env_get_u8_at_0x64

ble_219_0c066f0c.description: Getter returning the byte at +0x64 of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0; the same byte selects the constant-4 path in ble_ctrl_env_get_mode_or_4. Called from 0c06dc56.

ble_219_0c066f1c.name: ble_ctrl_env_get_u8_at_0x40
ble_219_0c066f1c.description: Getter returning the byte at +0x40 of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0, directly next to the 6-byte public address field at env+0x38. Called from 0c06cdb8.

ble_219_0c066f2c.name: ble_ctrl_env_get_u16_at_0x56
ble_219_0c066f2c.description: Getter returning the halfword at +0x56 of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0. Always paired with ble_ctrl_env_get_flag_bit6_at_0x18e by callers 0c06ca3c, 0c06caf4 and 0c06ed64.

ble_219_0c066f3c.name: ble_ctrl_env_set_peer_addr

ble_219_0c066f60.description: Copies the u32 at env+0x38 and the u16 at env+0x3c of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0 into the 6-byte buffer param_1. This is the controller's local Bluetooth device address (BD_ADDR). Called from 0c051eb8 and 0c05a8a0.

ble_219_0c067148.name: ble_ctrl_env_set_u8_at_0x42
ble_219_0c067148.description: Setter storing param_1 into +0x42 of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0. Called from 0c058250 along with ble_ctrl_env_set_u8_at_0x45 and ble_ctrl_env_set_peer_addr.

ble_219_0c067158.description: Setter storing param_1 into +0x45 of the controller environment struct pointed to by the RAM pointer DAT_200190d0. Called from 0c058250.

ble_219_0c06c090.name: ble_hook_table_register
ble_219_0c06c090.summary: Install the hook table and reset the hook period counter
ble_219_0c06c090.description: Initialises the global hook state: DAT_2001931c (call counter) = 0, DAT_20019318 (period) = -1 (periodic callback disabled), DAT_20019314 (hook table pointer) = param_1 and DAT_20019320 (enable flag) = 1. Called once from 0c0592a4. The table holds three function pointers used by ble_hook_invoke4 and ble_hook_invoke_indexed.

params.name: param_1
params.description: hook table: [0] periodic callback, [1] main hook(a,b,c,d), [2] indexed hook(idx,arg)

ble_219_0c06c090.notes: Table layout inferred from its two consumers; likely a debug/trace or profiling hook.

ble_219_0c06c0c0.name: ble_hook_invoke4
ble_219_0c06c0c0.summary: Call the registered 4-argument hook, optionally ticking a periodic callback first
ble_219_0c06c0c0.description: Does nothing unless the hook table pointer DAT_20019314 is non-NULL, table[1] is non-NULL and the enable byte DAT_20019320 is set. If the period DAT_20019318 is positive, the counter DAT_2001931c is compared with it: when counter >= period and table[0] is non-NULL the counter is cleared and table[0]() is called; afterwards the counter is incremented. It then tail-calls table[1](param_1..param_4). Used from a dozen or more call sites across the controller, so it behaves like a trace/log or event-notify entry point.
ble_219_0c06c0c0.notes: Purpose (logging vs profiling) is a guess.

ble_219_0c06c138.name: ble_hook_invoke_indexed
ble_219_0c06c138.summary: Call hook table entry 2 for channel idx (<3) if that channel is enabled
ble_219_0c06c138.description: Requires DAT_20019314 non-NULL, param_1 < 3, the per-index enable byte at DAT_20004998[param_1] non-zero and table[2] (offset 8) non-NULL; then calls table[2](param_1, param_2). Otherwise returns silently. Has a very large number of callers (04ace4, 04af00, 04bc2c, 04cdf0 ...), so likely a per-category trace/event notification.

params.name: param_2
params.description: argument passed through to the hook

ble_219_0c06c1e4.name: ble_ctrl_noop_callback
ble_219_0c06c1e4.summary: Empty function used as a no-op callback
ble_219_0c06c1e4.description: Consists of a single return instruction; it takes no arguments and has no side effects. It has no direct callers and is presumably stored in a function-pointer table as a placeholder.

ble_219_0c06c298.name: ble_ctrl_iface_probe_and_start
ble_219_0c06c298.summary: Call ops[1]; if it returns 0, set start flags and call ops[8](buf, 1)

If that call returns 0, it clears DAT_20019448, sets the flag bytes DAT_2001932a and DAT_20019328 to 1, calls the function at offset 0x20 of the table with (&DAT_20019334, 1) and finally sets DAT_2001944a = 1. Returns the first call's result. No direct callers (used via a pointer table).

returns.description: result of ops[1](); 0 means the start sequence was executed

ble_219_0c06c298.notes: Table identity unknown; may be an init/open style routine of a peripheral driver.

ble_219_0c06ca0c.name: ble_ctrl_opcode_in_set
ble_219_0c06ca0c.summary: Return 1 if opcode param_1 is in a fixed set and flag bit 15 of param_2 is clear
ble_219_0c06ca0c.description: If bit 15 of param_2 is clear, a switch on param_1 returns 1 for the values 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 14, 0x14, 0x17 and 0x18, otherwise (or when bit 15 is set) it returns 0. The value set resembles a list of control-PDU/command opcodes, but this is not confirmed. No direct callers.

params.name: param_2

ble_219_0c06ca0c.notes: Opcode meaning (LL control vs LMP vs internal message) unknown.

ble_219_0c06ee5c.name: ble_ctrl_get_max_data_len
ble_219_0c06ee5c.description: Returns 0xfb = 251, the maximum LE data PDU payload length allowed by Bluetooth 4.2+ data length extension. No side effects; no direct callers (used as a callback).

ble_219_0c06ee60.name: ble_ctrl_get_data_len_or_default

ble_219_0c06f450.name: sqrtf
ble_219_0c06f450.description: Two-instruction wrapper that executes the Cortex-M33 FPU vsqrt.f32 instruction on the argument and returns. Called from 0c06f288, a floating point routine in the same math cluster.

ble_219_0c06f460.name: __aeabi_dsub
ble_219_0c06f460.summary: Double-precision subtraction entry: negate the second operand and fall into __aeabi_dadd
ble_219_0c06f460.description: Single instruction that flips the sign bit of the high word of the second operand (EOR with 0x80000000) and then falls through into __aeabi_dadd at 0x0c06f464. The decompiler merged the two routines, so the body shown here is actually the whole dadd implementation after the sign flip (a - b = a + (-b)). Called from 0c06f2cc.

returns.description: a - b as IEEE-754 double (low word in r0, high in r1)

ble_219_0c06f464.name: __aeabi_dadd
ble_219_0c06f464.description: ARM runtime (libgcc/RVCT style) double add working on register pairs. Handles NaN, infinity and zero cases, aligns the smaller operand by the exponent difference (returning the larger one outright when the difference exceeds 0x36), negates operands according to sign, adds the 53-bit mantissas with carry, normalises using LZCOUNT and rounds to nearest-even, with overflow to infinity (0x7ff00000) and denormal handling. Called from 0c059b60, 0c06f2cc and 0c06f720.

ble_219_0c06f9ac.name: __aeabi_dmul_special_case
ble_219_0c06f9ac.summary: Slow path of double multiply: NaN/Inf/zero/denormal operand handling
ble_219_0c06f9ac.description: Not a standalone function: it is the out-of-line tail of the soft-float double multiply (called from 0c06f7d0 and 0c06fb92), which relies on registers set by its caller (unaffected r4/r12 hold exponent flags). If an operand is Inf/NaN it returns a quiet NaN (OR 0x7ff80000_00000000) or infinity with the XOR of the signs (invalid Inf*0 gives NaN); if an operand is zero it returns a signed zero; for denormal inputs it normalises the mantissa by shifting left until bit 20 of the high word is set.

returns.description: special-case result or normalised first operand

ble_219_0c06f9ac.notes: Decompiler shows register-passed state (unaff_r4/in_r12); exact handling of the continuation cannot be read from C.

ble_219_0c06fc04.name: __cmpdf2
ble_219_0c06fc04.summary: Soft-float double compare returning -1/0/1 (1 if unordered)
ble_219_0c06fc04.description: Compares two IEEE-754 doubles given as register pairs. If either is NaN (exponent all ones with non-zero mantissa) it returns 1. Treats +0 and -0 as equal and returns 0 for equal values; otherwise returns -1 or 1 according to sign-magnitude ordering (the result is (sign mask) | 1). Called by the wrapper at 0c06fc90.

returns.description: -1 if a<b, 0 if equal, 1 if a>b or unordered

ble_219_0c06fd04.name: __unorddf2
ble_219_0c06fd04.summary: Return 1 if either double operand is NaN
ble_219_0c06fd04.description: Checks whether the exponent (bits 62..52 after sign removal) of either operand is 0x7ff with a non-zero mantissa. Returns 1 when at least one is NaN (unordered) and 0 otherwise. Called by 0c06f220.

ble_219_0c06fd30.name: __aeabi_d2iz
ble_219_0c06fd30.summary: Convert double to signed 32-bit integer, truncating toward zero with saturation
ble_219_0c06fd30.description: Soft-float double to int conversion. Values with magnitude below 1 return 0, NaN returns 0, and overflow/infinity saturate to 0x7fffffff (positive) or 0x80000000 (negative). Otherwise the 53-bit mantissa is shifted right by (0x3e1 - exponent field adjust) and negated for negative input. Called from 0c059b60.

ble_219_0c06fd80.name: __aeabi_d2f
ble_219_0c06fd80.summary: Convert double to single-precision float (round to nearest-even)
ble_219_0c06fd80.description: Soft-float narrowing conversion. Detects Inf/NaN (returns 0x7fc00000 quiet NaN or signed infinity 0x7f800000), flushes to signed zero when the value is far below the float denormal range, builds denormals by shifting the mantissa with a sticky bit, otherwise re-biases the exponent and packs sign/exponent/mantissa with round-to-nearest-even (clearing the LSB on an exact tie). Callers: 0c035900, 0c059b60.

ble_219_0c06fef0.name: __udivmoddi4
ble_219_0c06fef0.summary: Unsigned 64-by-64 bit divide returning quotient and storing remainder
ble_219_0c06fef0.description: Software long division used by __aeabi_uldivmod style wrappers (callers 0c06fe20 and 0c06fec0). The dividend is param_2:param_1, the divisor param_4:param_3. For a 32-bit divisor it normalises with LZCOUNT and does two 16-bit-digit steps with correction (the classic Knuth/ARM scheme); a zero divisor raises an undefined-instruction trap (software_udf 0xff). For a 64-bit divisor it estimates the quotient from the top word, multiplies back and corrects by one. If param_5 is non-NULL the 64-bit remainder is written to param_5[0..1].
